newsitem.title: INDIA: India nationalists flay plan on foreign airlines.
newsitem.headline: India nationalists flay plan on foreign airlines.

text.p: India's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Thursday attacked Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front government for a plan that envisaged foreign airlines taking equity in domestic carriers.

BJP secretary general Pramod Mahajan said a preliminary draft of civil aviation policy prepared by Gujral's government permitted foreign airlines to take equity stakes of up to 40 percent in domestic carriers.
He distributed copies of the draft to reporters at a news conference.

"The most surprising and shocking part is that this draft is almost an about turn of the new civil aviation policy adopted and announced by the government of India just a few months back," Mahajan told reporters.
The civil aviation policy adopted by former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government in April specifically bars foreign airlines from holding stakes in Indian domestic carriers.
Mahajan said the provision would turn the clock back. "It is a mockery of the entire decision-making system," he added.

He said the draft had been circulated for discussion among India's top civil servants in charge of aviation, as well as to the chairmen of state-run domestic and international carriers, Indian Airlines and Air-India, respectively.
Mahajan called for a parliamentary discussion of the draft policy at the forthcoming monsoon session.
